newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Rebel car bombs rock city in northern Colombia. [CORRECTED 16:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Rebel car bombs rock city in northern Colombia. [CORRECTED 16:00 GMT]

text.p: Leftist rebels detonated two car bombs and attacked three police sentry posts early on Monday in Cucuta, capital of Colombia's northeast province of Norte de Santander, authorities said.
(Corrects to make clear Cucuta is provincial capital)

The back-to-back car bombs, which exploded shortly after midnight on Sunday, caused serious damage to the city's main brewery and to a branch office of Banco Ganadero, the country's leading commercial bank, police and municipal officials said.

They said suspected National Liberation Army (ELN) rebels set off the bombs and later stole several taxis for use in hit-and-run attacks on three police sentry posts across the city. Four policemen were injured in the attacks.
The ELN, Colombia's second leading guerrilla group, was founded by radical Roman Catholic priests in 1966.
The country's top guerrilla group, the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC), was blamed earlier for executing five people on Sunday in a rural area of northwestern Antioquia province.

Police said a squad of about 40 FARC rebels paraded residents of the small town of Liborina into the town's main square where they accused a municipal official and four peasants of collaborating with the military.
The five were then summarily executed as townspeople watched in horror, police said. They said the guerrillas subsequently retreated into the surrounding countryside.
